The *Rājaputtapetavatthu* (Pv 42), translated as "The Ghost Princes," is a narrative poem preserved in the *Petavatthu* of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text illustrates the karmic consequences of unwholesome actions, relating the fate of a prince who committed misdeeds against a Pacceka Buddha [SuttaCentral]. The work is listed with five translations in five modern languages on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

While SuttaCentral lists no curated parallels in other Buddhist traditions for this text [SuttaCentral], automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus reveals significant Pali-internal correspondence with the commentary, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, across 14 matching segments totaling 3,270 shared characters (including §1.1–14.1) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated alignments, DharmaNexus also identifies potential textual matches with Tibetan texts, most notably the *Mahāsūtrasamuccaya-nāma* (D3961; score 65) and to a lesser extent the *Ārya-daśasāhasrikā-prajñāpāramitā-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra* (D0011-2) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
